question: When is knowership properly attributed if it depends on a knowable?
premises: True knowership is not that which depends on a pure knowable and so on.
In such a dependent state, knowership is still spoken of.
It is spoken of only by force of fitness or suitability.
inference: Dependent knowership is a conventional attribution, not the ultimate nature of the knower.
plain_english: Knowership is not truly that state in which one depends on a pure knowable and other such factors. In that condition it is called knowership only in a secondary sense, because of suitability.
